title: The End-to-End Principle: Why Security Isn't Built Into the Network
explainer: In an influential paper first articulated in 1981 and published in its best-known form in 1984, Jerome Saltzer, David Reed, and David Clark argued that features like reliability and security should live at the communicating endpoints rather than inside the network's routers - a design choice known as the end-to-end principle. That deliberate decision is a big part of why IP and TCP, the protocols this lesson covers, carry no built-in encryption or authentication, and why security has to be layered on afterward through things like TLS, VPNs, and firewalls.
